subject: Cannot coerce class "structure("telemetry", package = "ctmm")" to a data.frame

messages.author: 73db0f7e944f4290
messages.subject: Cannot coerce class "structure("telemetry", package = "ctmm")" to a data.frame
parts:
Hi Chris,

I'm starting to learn how to use ctmm in R to estimate occurrence distributions via kriging and have an strange problem I don't know how to fix. After I import one animal's location data as a telemetry object with as.telemetry(), then try to make a basic plot, I get the error below.

> wht11_tel <- as.telemetry(object = wht11_df, timeformat = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", timezone = "America/New_York",
                          projection = "+proj=utm +zone=16 +ellps=GRS80 +towgs84=0,0,0,0,0,0,0 +units=m +no_defs",
                          UERE = wht11_df$hdop)
Maximum speed of 0.411 m/s observed in unknown
Minimum sampling interval of 58 minutes in unknown
Warning message:
In as.telemetry.data.frame(object = wht11_df, timeformat = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S",  :
  No MoveBank identification found. Assuming data corresponds to one indiviudal.
> plot(wht11_tel) 
Error in as.data.frame.default(x[[i]], optional = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = stringsAsFactors) : 
  cannot coerce class "structure("telemetry", package = "ctmm")" to a data.frame

I ignored the as.telemetry() warning message, since the data does indeed correspond to one individual. Anyways, what 's odd is that I successfully imported & plotted this animal's data just yesterday with the same code. Even the example provided in Calabrese et al.'s (2016) MEE paper is giving me the same error when it didn't before.

> data("buffalo")
> cilla <- buffalo[[1]]
> plot(cilla)
Error in as.data.frame.default(x[[i]], optional = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = stringsAsFactors) : 
  cannot coerce class "structure("telemetry", package = "ctmm")" to a data.frame

I get the same error when I try to run variogram() on wht11_tel, so I can't go on with the rest of my analysis . I don't think I'm making any coding errors & the last person who reported this problem inexplicably had the issue resolve itself overnight, so any ideas what's going on?

Thanks in advance!
-Emily Dinh

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Cannot coerce class "structure("telemetry", package = "ctmm")" to a data.frame
parts:
Hi Emily,

Have you tried uninstalling ctmm, restarting R without saving the workspace/session, and installing ctmm again? Also, with a recent versions of R (and ctmm from GitHub). Maybe a reboot too if running Windows.

98% of the time, weird errors like this (missing functions and cannot coerce class) go away afterwards. No idea what causes it.

Best,
Chris

messages.author: ec946d16b0c85849
messages.subject: Re: Cannot coerce class "structure("telemetry", package = "ctmm")" to a data.frame
parts:
It's possible some global variables saved in workspace overrides some functions in package.
You can try to locate the problem by loading different sections of workspace and check which caused the problem, and further divide that section until find the cause.

Or try to use more specific names for variables/function names. The common names/good names often were taken by package functions.
